newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Lebanon, South Korea to sign investment accords.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon, South Korea to sign investment accords.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafiq al-Hariri, in South Korea to seek help in rebuilding his country, said on Friday the two nations would sign agreements to avoid double taxation and protect investments.
Hariri told a news conference the accords would be signed in a few months. They were the outcome of his meeting earlier in the day with President Kim Young-sam.
"We are rebuilding our country, and we want to rebuild our industry. And I think Korean industries can participate," Hariri said.
"The opportunity is there for them," he added. "They have to come and participate and bid. And if they have the lowest price they will get the job."
Hariri said he had met construction industry leaders during his three-day visit, but declined to give details.
South Korea exported $130 million dollars worth of goods to Lebanon last year and imported Lebanese goods worth less than $4 million, Hariri said.
